subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Bestseller Lists and Bandwagons
description: A quick win: understand Bestseller Lists and Bandwagons.

hook.text: A book hits a bestseller list and sales double overnight. The label itself became the reason people bought it.

buildup.text: Bestseller labels create a bandwagon effect. Knowing others chose something makes it feel safer and more valuable.

discovery.text: Salganik's experiment randomized which songs appeared popular. Perceived popularity, not actual quality, drove future.

twist.text: Publishers have gamed bestseller lists by bulk-buying their own books. The label can be manufactured, not earned.

climax.text: Popularity is a signal but not proof of quality. When a bestseller label influences you, check if the content matches.

punchline.text: Bestsellers sell more because they are bestsellers.

quiz.question: What did Salganik's music experiment demonstrate?
options: Perceived popularity, not quality, drove future downloads
